questions.question: transform: translate(10px, 20px) moves an element:
questions.explanation: translate(x, y): positive x is right, positive y is down. Transforms are visual only — they don't affect surrounding layout.

questions.question: transform-origin controls:

options.text: The point around which rotate/scale/skew operations happen

questions.explanation: Default origin is center; changing it (e.g. top left) changes how rotation/scaling pivots.

questions.question: transform: scale(1.5) makes the element:

options.text: 1.5× its size (visual only, layout space unchanged)

questions.explanation: scale multiplies dimensions visually; surrounding layout is unaffected (unlike width/height which reflows).

questions.question: Multiple transforms on one element are applied:

options.text: Right-to-left as a combined matrix (e.g. translate then rotate order matters)

questions.explanation: transform: translate() rotate() applies right-to-left; order changes the result (rotate-then-translate differs from translate-then-rotate).

questions.question: transform: rotate(45deg) rotates:
questions.explanation: Positive angles rotate clockwise (in standard screen coords). Negative rotates counter-clockwise.

questions.question: A transform creates a new:

options.text: Stacking context and containing block (affects fixed descendants)

questions.explanation: Applying transform establishes a stacking context and a containing block — so position:fixed children anchor to it, not the viewport.

questions.question: To flip horizontally you use:
questions.explanation: scaleX(-1) mirrors along the X axis. rotate(180) flips both axes; for horizontal-only use scaleX(-1).

questions.question: Transforms are GPU-friendly because they:

options.text: Run on the compositor layer (no layout/paint per frame)

questions.explanation: translate/rotate/scale/opacity animate on the compositor — that's why they're the preferred animation properties for smoothness.
